gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-004 identifies the same failed identity used in the random-walk Fair-SMW theorem: invertibility of D^{-1} preserves rank but does not preserve the relevant row space or projection invariance. It supplies the required range condition, a counterexample, and the resulting failure of the claimed real-spectrum conclusion.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both the gold issue and ISSUE-004 diagnose the invalid inference that multiplying F^T by an invertible diagonal matrix makes its row space invariant under the fairness projection. Consequently, the identity F^T D^{-1}=F^T D^{-1}P_F and the subsequent symmetric-similarity/real-spectrum argument fail, so the unconditional theorem is false.

component_coverage.gold_component: The proof incorrectly infers the projection identity and real-spectrum theorem from invertibility of D^{-1}; the relevant row-space invariance can fail, including on an admissible irregular example.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-004 explicitly distinguishes preservation of column space from the required row-space/range invariance, gives an irregular-graph counterexample, and states that the simplification and claimed similarity—and hence realness of the eigenvalues—are unjustified. This independently diagnoses the full substantive gold defect.
